children: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Federal Reserve officials to remain flexible on interest rates, arguing that productivity gains from artificial intelligence and deregulation could allow the US economy to grow faster without generating significantly more inflation.

Bessent pointed to the strong economy under President Donald Trump, crediting tax cuts and reduced regulation for supporting growth. At the same time, higher fuel costs stemming from the Iran conflict have complicated the inflation outlook ahead of the November midterm elections.
, Bessent said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh recognizes parallels between the current productivity boom and the internet-driven expansion of the 1990s under former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan “let things run,” and “the board and the voters on the Fed should have an open mind because, again, it’s the deregulatory aspect,” Bessent said.

For investors, Bessent’s comments highlight the debate at the center of the interest-rate outlook. If AI and deregulation are raising the economy’s productive capacity, the Fed may have more room to tolerate strong growth without responding with aggressive rate increases. That could support stocks and other risk assets. But persistently high energy prices could keep inflation elevated, potentially pushing Treasury yields higher and keeping pressure on rate-sensitive sectors.

The Fed is already confronting conflicting signals. Core consumer prices rose 0.3% in August and were up 2.4% from a year earlier. The central bank subsequently raised its benchmark interest rate for the first time since 2023.
Bessent nevertheless argued that “core inflation has been very quiescent, and is has actually dropped over the past few months.”

Energy remains a major source of uncertainty. Higher gasoline and diesel prices tied to the Iran war and attacks on Russian energy infrastructure have contributed to inflation pressures and elevated global bond yields.
Bessent also addressed China’s relationship with Iran, saying he expects Iranian oil shipments to China to end soon as Washington increases economic pressure on Tehran.

“China has substantially reduced any assistance to Iran” and “there’s only 15 million more barrels of Iranian oil on the water,” he said. “Probably within the next two weeks they’re going to make their final delivery of oil to China and then they will have nothing.”

Bessent’s comments come as the Trump administration seeks to isolate Iran economically and increase pressure on Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also recently asked Chinese President Xi Jinping to halt assistance to Iran.

title: Bessent urges Fed to keep ‘open mind’ on rates as AI boosts productivity
